methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Redwood Materials, a Series D climate and energy company founded by J.B. Straubel, has raised $2.125B to date and carries a current post-money valuation of $6.0B+. The relevant comp universe comprises 1 public company and 8 private peers across climate technology and adjacent energy sectors, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods were triangulated. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement, yielding $9.0B from the $6.0B last post-money valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, Amogy at $700M) produces a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The divergence reflects stage and business model differences among peers; KoBold trades at a premium while Amogy and Electric Hydrogen command lower valuations.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $850M (conservative floor) to $10.3B (aggressive ceiling), with a median estimate of $5.0B. The current $6.0B valuation sits above the peer-derived median but below the stage-progression upper bound, suggesting modest premium to cohort. Key uncertainties include capital intensity through commercialization, battery recycling technology differentiation relative to peers, and near-term cash burn trajectory given the capital-intensive nature of climate hardware deployment.
